Lemma
[Backward lower derivative of the distance function] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0063, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0064 1. ch18:18.4\group Changing Distances

If $g(t)$ is a smooth family of complete metrics, then, in the sense of the lower backward derivative, \[ \left.\frac{\partial _-}{\partial t}\right|_{t=t_0}d_{g(t)}(x,x_0) \ge \frac12\max _{\eta \in \mathcal Z(t_0)} \int _\eta \partial _tg(t_0)(\eta ',\eta ')\, \dd s. \]
Proof

\sketch For every $g(t_0)$-minimizing geodesic $\eta $, one has $L_{g(t)}(\eta )\ge d_{g(t)}(x,x_0)$ for earlier times and equality at $t_0$. Taking the lower backward derivative and applying the first variation formula for length gives the asserted inequality for each $\eta $; maximizing over the compact set $\mathcal Z(t_0)$ completes the proof.

□
